To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the levels of circulating HSP60 are partly genetically controlled, are related to the levels of total and LDL cholesterol, are related to psychological stress and are stable over time in healthy individuals.
the circulating levels of heat shock protein 10 are associated with psychological, biological, genetic, and lifestyle factors that are also known to influence cardiovascular disease risk.

Plasma Hsp60 levels are associated with cardiovascular risk factors and are partly genetically determined, and that the association of plasma Hsp70 levels with cardiovascular risk factors may reflect the presence of atherosclerosis and not be causative.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of psychobiological factors, particularly stress, in the development of cardiovascular disease.

the identification and quantification of plasma Hsp70 and Hsp60 and the investigation of the role of psychophysiological and genetic factors in the regulation of these proteins in healthy and diseased individuals.
understanding the relationship between stress, the immune system, and the cardiovascular system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
plasma heat shock protein 90 (Hsp90) levels are associated with the risk of developing cardiovascular disease and this is mediated by a variety of biological and psychological factors.
the Hsp60 levels are associated with a number of risk factors for coronary heart disease, including psychological distress, low emotional support, and high job demand.
plasma Hsp60 is associated with cardiovascular disease and that this is mediated by psychosocial factors, biological factors, and genetic factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Hsp60 levels may be a useful biomarker of coronary artery disease, particularly in individuals with diabetes.
the levels of Hsp60 in the circulation are related to the degree of psychological distress, the extent of the inflammatory process, and genetic factors.
the plasma levels of Hsp60 are related to a range of biological, psychosocial and genetic factors that are known to increase the risk of cardiovascular disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Hsp60 levels are associated with psychological stress in healthy men.

the levels of circulating heat shock protein 90 (Hsp90) and heat shock protein 27 (Hsp27) are elevated in patients with coronary heart disease and that these heat shock proteins may have important roles in cardiovascular disease pathogenesis.
plasma levels of Hsp60 are a marker for coronary artery disease risk.
